ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Other One, epic Lovelight and tight Phil bass drive show
ai_show_review.blurb: The concert bursts open with a smoking The Other One and an explosive Turn On Your Lovelight. Not Fade Away flows seamlessly into Greatest Story Ever Told and Playing In The Band, while Phil’s bass stays prominently in charge. The soundboard source is crisp and balanced despite a few tape‑flip hiccups.
ai_show_review.review: April 12, 1971 at the Civic Arena finds the Dead riding a high‑energy wave that never quite lets up. After a tentative first set that tightens by Bertha, the second set launches with a fiery Truckin' that segues into Bill Kreutzmann’s white‑hot drumming on The Other One. Jerry fires up his guitar and vocals, delivering strong riffs while occasional lyric slips on Loser add a human touch. Phil Lesh is unmistakably in high gear, his bass anchoring the sprawling jams and leading the charge through the Not Fade Away → Greatest Story Ever Told → Playing In The Band sequence. Bob Weir’s rhythm work locks in tightly, especially on Hard To Handle and Johnny B. Goode, even though the former suffers a mid‑song cut. Pigpen’s keyboards sit quietly in the mix, typical of this era, while Bill’s drumming on Turn On Your Lovelight is both tight and explosive. The Miller soundboard capture delivers crystal‑clear instrument separation with the audience barely audible, offering an excellent listening experience despite minor tape glitches in Cold Rain And Snow and a cut in Hard To Handle.

best_recording.reason: Crisp soundboard mix with clear instrument separation; captures the high‑energy performance while minimizing tape glitches.
